metadata.title: ORCHID phase registry (binary systems)
metadata.description:
ORCHID phase registry (binary systems), version 0: one entry per phase of each binary system, with every name the phase goes by, the CALPHAD models that describe it, where calculated phase diagrams make it stable, example literature references, and a crystal-structure type assigned only when certain. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10.

What

  • phases/registry.json: 10,496 phases in 1,241 binary systems; id phase:<sorted elements>:<slug> (the SGTE-corpus canonical convention). Names in namespaces tdb (TDB file and phase name), paper (DOI and printed label), corpus, mp, oqmd: 43,251 names.
  • Models: 22,556 TDB phase declarations (file SHA-256, sublattices, site ratios, constituents) from the bundled SGTE binary collection; stability ranges per calculated diagram; literature value counts; up to 10 example references per phase (assessments first) with DOI and role.
  • Structure: 6,259 phases assigned from the standard phase name (tier A), 150 from a unique Materials Project + OQMD on-hull match (tier B, "DFT-supported"), 1,253 assessment-declared (tier C, assessor-stated: exactly one consistent structure in the Hallstedt 2025 crystallographic table for that phase name and system), 1,305 liquid and 231 gas; 1,240 phases carry review candidates and are marked needs_review.
  • TDB definitions: every model carries the verbatim PHASE, CONSTITUENT and TYPE_DEFINITION statements with line numbers, a parsed view (type codes, sublattices, site ratios, constituents with major-constituent markers, magnetic model, order/disorder partner), parameter counts by kind and interaction order (no expressions), and links to the TDB file.
  • phases/structure_types.json: 1,563 structure types (prototype, Strukturbericht, Pearson symbol, space group), each with its source; also registry.csv, registry.parquet, registry.jsonld (schema.org DefinedTermSet), review_queue.json, CONFLICTS.md, SCHEMA.md.

How

Deterministic builder (tools/build_phase_registry.py, standard library) over the bundled TDB files, the Hallstedt 2025 crystallographic table, the ORCHID SGTE-corpus phase mappings and literature values, the calculated binary phase diagrams and the Materials Project / OQMD hull layers. No model or network calls.

Limitations

  • A structure type is assigned only when certain or, for tier C, as stated by the assessment's crystallographic table; everything else is a review candidate, not a claim.
  • DFT entries are computed 0 K structures, not the CALPHAD phase; tier B requires agreement of both databases and a unique structure type for the space group and stoichiometry.
  • Paper labels come from machine-extracted literature values (Version 1); mapping basis is recorded per name.
  • Binary systems only; stability comes from calculated (not measured) diagrams.

Licence

Derived data: CC BY 4.0. Third-party data keep their own licences and citations (NOTICE.md, LICENSES.md in the bundle): SGTE binary collection and its crystallographic table, Hallstedt 2025 (CC BY 4.0); Materials Project (CC BY 4.0); OQMD (CC BY 4.0).

Files: one zip (orchid-phase-registry-v2026.10.zip) holding the files at their repository paths, a MANIFEST.sha256, the README, CHANGELOG and licence files. Its file list with sizes and SHA-256 is zenodo/phase-registry.files.json in the data repository.

Saal et al., JOM 65 (2013) 1501, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4 and S. Kirklin et al., npj Comput.
